title: 1973 AHSME Problem 11
statement:
A circle with a circumscribed and an inscribed square centered at the origin \(O\) of a rectangular coordinate system with positive \(x\)- and \(y\)-axes \(OX\) and \(OY\) is shown in each figure \(\mathrm{I}\) to \(\mathrm{IV}\) below.

The inequalities \[ \begin{aligned} |x|+|y| &\le \sqrt{2(x^2+y^2)}\\ &\le 2\operatorname{Max}(|x|,|y|). \end{aligned} \] are represented geometrically by the figure numbered

Geometric representation: An inequality \(f(x,y)\le g(x,y)\) for all \(x,\) \(y\) is represented by a figure showing, for a typical real number \(a,\) the containment \[ \begin{aligned} &\{(x,y):g(x,y)\le a\}\\ &\quad\subset \{(x,y):f(x,y)\le a\}. \end{aligned} \]

solutions.text:
For a fixed positive \(a,\) the set \[ 2\operatorname{Max}(|x|,|y|)\le a \] is an axis-aligned square. The set \[ \sqrt{2(x^2+y^2)}\le a \] is its circumscribed circle, and \[ |x|+|y|\le a \] is the diamond circumscribed about that circle. Thus the required nesting is an inner axis-aligned square, then a circle, then an outer diamond, which is figure \(\mathrm{II}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Identify the shapes of the sublevel sets for \(|x|+|y|,\) \(\sqrt{2(x^2+y^2)},\) and \(2\operatorname{Max}(|x|,|y|)\)
The inequality reverses the order of containment of the corresponding sublevel sets
